result.title: What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports
result.summary: Human supervisors rely on coding agents' reports to assess progress, verify repairs, and decide when to intervene. But a supervisor cannot investigate a failure they were never told occurred. Failed attempts, workarounds, and unresolved risks may disappear from routine reports, leaving supervisors unaware of issues that warrant scrutiny. We conduct CTXGAP, a measurement study quantifying the gap in task-state recoverability between agents' accumulated user-facing reports and their full recorded execution contexts. Across 37 coding tasks and 4,799 valid probes, agents answer 93.6% of task-state questions on demand; full-context readers recover 92.7%, while report-only readers recover 52.0%, a 40.7-point gap. At the final checkpoints of 30 verified fixes, the gap remains 34.8 points. Human annotation identifies states mentioned without enough supporting detail as the largest category of unrecovered information, and model-assessed supervision-relevant states retain substantial gaps. Full terminal scrollback improves recovery to 73.6% but still trails full context. Under matched report lengths, context-informed rewrites improve recovery by about eight points, without a detectable targeted-over-natural advantage. Positive gaps persist across harnesses and independent DeepSeek execution and measurement. CTXGAP establishes report-based task-state recoverability as a complementary evaluation dimension.

AI.brief_summary: CTXGAP 测量编码代理在 37 个任务、4799 次探针中，其面向用户的报告与完整执行上下文之间在任务状态可恢复性上的差距（全上下文 92.7% 对仅报告 52.0%），并检验终端回滚、报告改写等缓解手段。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「内部状态经有限输出通道后有多大可恢复性」的探针式测量，可能为 LVR 中判断答案是否真正使用 latent 内容、以及轨迹监督信息是否丢失提供评价视角，但论文属编码代理领域、不含视觉或多模态推理，联系尚需核查。
